paper.title_en: A differentiable neural-field forward model for cosmic-ray muon scattering tomography
paper.abstract_en: Cosmic-ray muon scattering tomography (MST) recovers the inverse radiation length <math altimg="si428.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1769"><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> of dense or shielded objects, but classical algorithms (PoCA, MLEM) discretise the volume into a fixed voxel grid and become noise-limited at fine resolution. We introduce MINT (Muon Implicit Neural Tomography), a differentiable neural-field framework that represents <math altimg="si257.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1802"><mi>λ</mi></math> by a coordinate-based network with multi-resolution hash encoding and optimises the per-track multiple Coulomb scattering log-likelihood end-to-end by stochastic gradient descent. Validated on two Geant4-based benchmarks spanning nuclear security and geophysical surveying, and on real detector data, MINT consistently outperforms MLEM in structural fidelity, dense-object segmentation, and background smoothness, while matching or exceeding its intensity accuracy in both the logarithmic and the linear domain. In a small-object detection study inside a full-scale ISO-like 20-foot container (twelve high-<math altimg="si286.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1811"><mi>Z</mi></math> cubes of decreasing size, 10–1 cm, exposed in air and concealed inside 30-cm-side steel cubes), at a fixed 0.5% background-voxel exceedance fraction MINT detects 10 of 12 objects — down to a 1 cm tungsten cube hidden in steel — versus 4 of 12 for both PoCA and MLEM; and when the grid is refined at fixed track budget PoCA and MLEM lose the targets while MINT still localises them. In a mine-tunnel ore-body survey (<math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1817"><mrow><mn>1000</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mn>800</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mn>400</mn></mrow></math> cm, 12.5 cm voxels, <math altimg="si5.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1835"><mrow><mn>1.6</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> tracks), MINT reduces the log-RMSE to 0.413 against 1.070 for MLEM and 1.895 for PoCA and the linear RMSE to 0.164 against 0.440 cm<sup loc="post">−1</sup>; under grid refinement at a fixed track budget its structural-fidelity advantage over MLEM widens from <math altimg="si6.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1858"><mrow><mo>×</mo><mn>1.3</mn></mrow></math> to <math altimg="si7.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1866"><mrow><mo>×</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> as PoCA and MLEM degrade to noise. Finally, on real data from the INFN Padova large-volume prototype (<math altimg="si8.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1875"><mrow><mn>1.26</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> cosmic-ray tracks, six material samples from Al to W), MINT with a Gaussian single-<math altimg="si9.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1895"><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></math> likelihood locates all six samples over a markedly cleaner background than MLEM and with slightly better reconstructed scattering densities, confirming the simulation results under real detector conditions. •MINT recovers inverse radiation length via multi-resolution hash-grid neural fields.•Closed-form Gaussian Highland NLL yields differentiable muon-track line integrals.•20-ft scan: MINT detects 10/12 high-Z cubes, even a 1-cm tungsten cube inside steel.•Ore-body test: MINT gives 0.413 log-RMSE and retains structure on 3.125-cm grids.•Experimental data: MINT finds all six Al-to-W samples on cleaner background than MLEM.
